question: A 27-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with minor injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident. He says that he is fine. He also witnessed the death of a teenage girl in the accident who was his sister’s friend. He is able to return to work within a few days. A month later, he presents being withdrawn and increasingly irritable. He says recently he has been experiencing depressed moods and higher anxiety than usual. He says that he feels guilty about the girl’s death, stating that he could have saved her if only he had acted quicker. He adds that he became extremely anxious while driving by a car accident on the freeway recently, and that, even when watching television or a movie, he feels panicked during a car crash scene. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Witnessed death of sister's friend in a motor vehicle accident -> Feelings of guilt and responsibility for the death -> Increased anxiety and depressed moods -> Panic during car crash scenes -> Post-traumatic stress disorder -> 80%

CHAIN: Minor injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident -> Witnessed death of sister's friend -> Survivor guilt and self-blame -> Increased anxiety and irritability -> Panic attacks triggered by reminders of the accident -> Post-traumatic stress disorder -> 85%

CHAIN: Witnessed death of sister's friend in a motor vehicle accident -> Survivor guilt and self-blame -> Increased anxiety and irritability -> Panic attacks triggered by reminders of the accident -> Re-experiencing trauma symptoms -> Post-traumatic stress disorder -> 90%
enhanced_information: The most likely diagnosis in this patient is Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) based on the chain of events starting from witnessing the death of his sister's friend in a motor vehicle accident, leading to survivor guilt, increased anxiety, irritability, and panic attacks triggered by reminders of the accident. This aligns with the symptoms and progression of PTSD. The evidence paths linking accidents to stress disorders, particularly post-traumatic stress, further support this diagnosis.
analysis: The patient's presentation of experiencing distressing symptoms following a traumatic event, survivor guilt, increased anxiety, irritability, and panic attacks triggered by reminders of the accident is highly suggestive of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). The enhanced information provided further supports this diagnosis based on the chain of events and symptom progression. PTSD is a common mental health condition that can develop after a person is exposed to a traumatic event, such as witnessing a death in a motor vehicle accident. The symptoms described align with the diagnostic criteria for PTSD.
